correctness.rationale: For every finite connected ON graph and subset OFF graph, the joint canonical stationary law is reversible and unique. Exact linear closure L_e f_h=f_{Q_e h}, together with the hypergeometric covariance coefficient k(n-k)/[n(n-1)], reduces the all-k integrated variance to an invertible vertex/gate Poisson problem. The OFF-kernel test vector yields the all-rate inequality. Schur complement on the OFF-component constant subspace has pI as its first-order coupling and produces the exact kappa inverse coefficient and iff boundedness. K_n eigenvectors provide the exact formula. Independent exact-rational full-state and reduced-generator calculations were run successfully, including disconnected/connected OFF cases and varied particle numbers; finite checks are corroboration only.
residual_risks: No result extends without reproof to state-dependent gate behavior, irreversible particle rates or the limit n tending to infinity.

value.rationale: The natural physical question is whether slowly reconnecting a disconnected transport network makes time-integrated particle-count fluctuations large despite speed-invariant stationary occupancy. The exact component projection gives a meaningful all-finite-graph sharp iff classification and computable density susceptibility for every k. The all-rate lower bound and exact complete-graph realization are reproducible benchmarks for dynamic-bottleneck coarse graining, not merely a renaming of a fixed static spectral gap. No phase-transition or thermodynamic-limit claim is needed.
residual_risks: Interpretation applies to stationary integrated linear observables and does not transfer to arbitrary higher cumulants or arbitrary dynamic-gate physics.
